findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has dead code and misleading semantics
findings.body: The function enableSqlExpressions always returns false because both the `if enabled` branch and the fallthrough return false, regardless of the feature flag value. The local variable `enabled` is the negation of FlagSqlExpressions, so the name reads as a double negative (`enabled := !IsEnabled(...)`). The net effect is just `return false`. This is a maintainability trap: a future developer trying to 'fix' the function to honor the feature flag will be misled by the dead branch and the variable naming, and could easily reintroduce SQL execution in a way that re-introduces CVE-2024-9264. The function should be a single explicit `return false` with a comment explaining the security reason, or the name should be changed to make the always-disabled behavior obvious.

findings.title: Misleading 'not implemented' error message
findings.body: The error returned when SQL expressions are rejected reads `sqlExpressions is not implemented`. SQL expressions were implemented previously; they are now intentionally disabled as the mitigation for CVE-2024-9264. The message will mislead users and operators (and make log/triage harder) into thinking the feature simply wasn't built, rather than that it was turned off for security. It should reference the security reason (e.g. 'sqlExpressions have been disabled due to CVE-2024-9264').

findings.title: Stub DB has no comment explaining why it exists
findings.body: The new file pkg/expr/sql/db.go replaces the vulnerable scottlepp/go-duck-backed implementation with a no-op stub. There is no package or type-level comment stating that this stub intentionally exists to neutralize CVE-2024-9264 and that the real SQL execution backend must not be re-introduced without addressing that vulnerability. Without such a comment, a future contributor is likely to delete the stub and reinstate DuckDB execution, silently re-exposing the RCE/LFI.

findings.title: Security-fix change to SQL expressions has no test coverage
findings.body: This PR is the public fix for CVE-2024-9264 and changes both the gating (reader.go now rejects QueryTypeSQL) and the SQL backend (db.go stub, parser.go, sql_command.go). No test file is added or updated to verify that: (1) a QueryTypeSQL request now returns the documented error from reader.go, (2) NewSQLCommand / UnmarshalSQLCommand cannot produce an executable SQLCommand, and (3) SQLCommand.Execute, if reached, returns an error instead of executing user-controlled SQL. Without regression tests it is very easy for a future change (e.g. 're-enable SQL via feature flag', or deleting the stub) to silently re-introduce the vulnerability. The PR description also leaves the feature-flag-related docs unchecked; a test asserting behavior under the flag would at least lock the mitigation down.
